findings.breaking_input: The checkout starts with a tracked file already dirty, as it does here (` M docs/session-log.md`). A benched model appends to or overwrites that file. Its porcelain line is still ` M docs/session-log.md`, so the digest is unchanged. The opposite case also breaks: the file starts clean and one of arc's own hooks appends to the tracked docs/session-log.md during the run. A ` M` line appears and the run is voided as 'the arc checkout moved' with no model write at all.
findings.why: Porcelain v1 reports only per-path status codes, never content. An edit to an already-dirty tracked file is invisible, which contradicts the ADR's claim that tracked edits are covered. A hook or another writer touching a clean tracked file looks identical to the model moving the checkout.
findings.fix: Hash the content of dirty tracked files, for example `git diff HEAD` piped through sha256 or `git hash-object` of each path listed by `diff --name-only HEAD`. Name hook-owned paths such as docs/session-log.md and exclude them explicitly, rather than relying on the status code.

findings.breaking_input: The arc checkout is a real repo, but `rev-parse --git-dir` fails for a reason other than 'not a repository': git missing from PATH (ENOENT), 'detected dubious ownership' (exit 128, common on Windows worktrees owned by another SID), or a corrupt .git. The fingerprint returns null both before and after, and two nulls compare equal. The run proceeds with containment silently unchecked.
findings.why: Every failure of the first call is folded into 'no repository', the same constant-for-a-failed-read pattern the PR claims to have closed. The unreadable path covers only failures after this first call. `checkoutMovedSince` retries only `.unreadable`, not null. A transient failure of this call on the later read is reported as 'moved' with '(no repo)'.
findings.fix: Return null only when git reports the not-a-repository case (exit 128 with that message, or `rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` giving a definite answer). Every other failure returns `{unreadable}`, and the null case retries too.
findings.twin_of: A failed read folded into a comparison as a constant

findings.breaking_input: `rev-parse --verify -q HEAD`, `symbolic-ref -q HEAD` or `reflog show` fails with something other than the expected exit 1 (a lock, a corrupt object, ENOBUFS on a long HEAD reflog past the execFileSync 1 MB default). The catch substitutes '(unborn)', '(detached)' or '' regardless of the cause.
findings.why: The fallback catches every error, not just the one the comment names. A failing reflog read silently drops the reflog from the digest, so the commit-then-reset-back coverage (L3/L6) vanishes with no signal. A transient HEAD failure becomes '(unborn)' on one read and the real SHA on the other, giving a false 'moved' with a misleading report. The reflog is the one unbounded read, and it is the one with a swallow-all fallback.
findings.fix: Apply a fallback only for the specific expected exit status (1 for `-q` probes), and let every other failure throw into `{unreadable}`. Raise maxBuffer for the reflog read, or cap it with `-n`.
findings.twin_of: A failed read folded into a comparison as a constant

findings.where: .claude/scripts/engine/arc-bench.mjs:1519-1521 (for-each-ref over all non-remote refs, and `worktree list --porcelain`)
findings.breaking_input: The arc checkout is a linked worktree (arc-bench-2 here), and the owner runs parallel sessions in sibling worktrees of the same repo. Another worktree commits or creates a branch, or any session runs `git fetch --tags`. refs/heads, refs/tags and the worktree list (which carries every worktree's HEAD SHA) all change during the run, so the digest changes and bench stops.
findings.why: The fingerprint scopes to the whole shared repository, not to this checkout. The ADR's 'needs the checkout to itself' consequence is understated: it means the whole repo, including every worktree and every tag fetch. Valid paid runs get voided, and the user has a standing workflow of parallel sessions.
findings.fix: Take the worktree list for this worktree only. Treat other worktrees' HEADs and branches as informational, or compare them as a separate non-fatal 'shared state moved' field. Exclude refs/tags from fetch-driven changes, or fingerprint them separately.

findings.where: .claude/scripts/engine/arc-bench.mjs:1794-1810 (the capture write happens before the `if (ck.moved)` break)
findings.breaking_input: Attempt k answers while working inside arc and moves the checkout. `ck.moved` is true, but the capture record is written first, as `${dir}/${k}.json`, with no contamination marker. A later `--replay` or `--capture` consumer reads that dir and scores the contaminated answer as a valid attempt.
findings.why: ADR-0916 says the partial runs are void and their captures are not evidence. The code still persists the contaminated attempt's capture, indistinguishable from a clean one, and the record carries no checkout state.
findings.fix: Skip writing the capture when `ck.moved`, or write it with `contaminated: true` plus the checkout move reason. Make replay refuse such records.

findings.breaking_input: ARC_WORK_ROOT names a directory that does not exist: a stale temp fixture, or an MSYS-style `/c/Users/...` value that `resolve()` turns into `C:\c\Users\...`. `spawn` with a nonexistent cwd fails with ENOENT.
findings.why: The drivers classify ENOENT as 'CLI not installed / driver unavailable', so a bad work root is reported as a missing CLI. B5 from round 1 asked to fail closed when the path is not an existing directory. The fix only normalised the path, so the misattribution remains. The `resolve()` also gives a relative value an absolute path that may differ from the cwd arc-run actually spawned in.
findings.fix: After `resolve`, `statSync(...).isDirectory()` and fail with a distinct 'work root does not exist' error before spawning. Assert that it equals `process.cwd()` unless the two are known to differ.

findings.breaking_input: The owner's own session or a hook runs `git commit` or `git add` in the same worktree at the moment bench's per-attempt `git status` refreshes the index. Plain `git status` takes `.git/index.lock` to write the refreshed index. The owner's command fails with 'Unable to create .../index.lock'.
findings.why: A read-only check mutates arc's index and holds the lock, so it can break the owner's concurrent git operation. On Windows with core.fsmonitor it can also start a per-worktree daemon.
findings.fix: Set `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0` in the environment of every fingerprint read, or use `git --no-optional-locks status`.

findings.breaking_input: A git read fails under execFileSync. The first line of `e.message` is 'Command failed: git -C <root> <args>', and the actual stderr reason is on the following lines. The retry in `checkoutMovedSince` runs back-to-back with no delay.
findings.why: The reported reason is the command line, not the failure, which is the pattern of taking one line of mixed output as the reason. A back-to-back retry cannot outlast a lock or a gc that holds for hundreds of milliseconds, so the 'transient lock' justification does not hold and a paid run still gets voided.
findings.fix: Report `e.stderr` trimmed to its first non-empty line, with the exit status. Sleep roughly 250-500 ms between the retries, and retry up to three times.
